solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son and I can sort out something for breakfast

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or askew, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent and child agree to make breakfast together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is the anagram's own fodder too: the letters of S, I, CAN and SORT are all shuffled together, with 'out' signalling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky crescent pastry, a typical item eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Old banger His Majesty devoured

blocks.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is King Charles's royal cipher
past tense of eat

explanation.surface: The King gobbled up an old sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, and also for a rickety old car; the clue wants the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is informal for a decrepit old vehicle, just as banger is.

clue.text: Suddenly under performing, Moo's beat

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed under another comes after it in the column

blocks.note: an act that is performing is on
Moo is the setter, so Moo's is I'm
a pulse is a rhythmic beat

explanation.surface: A drummer called Moo suddenly loses the beat while underperforming.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Moo, so 'Moo's' stands for I'M. 'Under performing' reads as one word, underperforming, but 'under' only places the second part below ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means acting without forethought, on a sudden whim.

clue.text: Restriction on amphetamine usage — 20 or 30 maybe?

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: speed is slang for amphetamine, so a cap on its use
second meaning: typical road limits in miles per hour

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading, since speed is street slang for amphetamine; the second is the everyday sense on British road signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed limits on British urban roads are commonly 20 or 30 miles per hour, the numbers printed on the signs.

clue.text: Helped a detective from the south to squash speculation

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upward runs the word backwards
squashing something in means pressing it inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
short for detective
a bet is a speculative wager

explanation.surface: A detective arriving from down south shuts down idle speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: A and the reversed detective together surround the speculation, which sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, so abetted is a synonym of helped.

clue.text: Sign nearly all our opponents will join attack

indicators.note: nearly all of a word means dropping its final letter

blocks.note: our opponents are them; drop the last letter
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A captain reads a signal that almost the whole opposing side is about to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a sign of the zodiac: Capricorn is the Goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, a zodiac sign, is known as the Goat.

clue.text: Listened to cry of the masses

indicators.note: a cry is something called out, so we hear the word rather than read it

blocks.note: the herd is a scornful term for the common people

explanation.surface: Someone paid attention to the clamour of the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Heard is the past tense of hear, meaning perceived or listened to.

clue.text: Suspend Chinese? Good

blocks.note: the Han are China's majority ethnic group
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether putting a Chinese item on hold would be good.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something is to suspend it from above.

clue.text: Grew weak and cried, losing weight

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: wailed means cried out in grief
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A patient weakened, wept and lost weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the W from WAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be ill or in poor health, so ailed suits grew weak.

clue.text: Recent ad you originally designed for care facility

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the start of the word
something designed is newly arranged, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of you

explanation.surface: An advertising firm's latest ad was created for a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: A day centre is a place providing daytime care and activities for elderly or disabled people.

clue.text: Hack in casualty, shot

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
a shot at something is an attempt, a bid

explanation.surface: A cyber attack hits the hospital's emergency department, leaving it in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' is not computing but the informal verb for tolerate, as in 'I can't hack it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack something, informally, is to cope with or put up with it, which is what abide means.

clue.text: Discourage daughter leaving new friend all the time

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
D is the abbreviation for daughter
N is the abbreviation for new
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A parent constantly discourages a daughter from leaving to see a new friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from DETER, then add N and ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever or constantly, an exaggerated way of saying always.

clue.text: Speed of march to South Pole?

blocks.note: first meaning: promptness, an old sense of the word
second meaning: an organised journey, such as Scott's or Amundsen's

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking how fast a polar march went; the first sense, quickness, is rarer and formal.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness in getting things done, and also an organised trek such as one to the Pole.

clue.text: Steal an advantage

blocks.note: first meaning: to creep or move stealthily
second meaning: a slight superiority over rivals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal an advantage' reads as one phrase about cheating; 'steal' here is to creep, not to thieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move gradually or stealthily, and an edge is a competitive lead over others.

clue.text: Cold-blooded creature alarms dean horribly

indicators.note: something done horribly is badly mangled, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reptile in the cathedral gives the dean a dreadful fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is an amphibian, and amphibians are cold-blooded animals.

clue.text: Flirted with copper getting married

blocks.note: D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin
allied means joined, as by marriage

explanation.surface: Someone flirted with a policeman and ended up wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but here it is the old penny, abbreviated D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to flirt or toy with someone in a light, non-serious way.

clue.text: Sought-after individual found in eccentric earl's bed

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of order
found in means located inside something else

blocks.note: I is one, a single individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sought-after person was discovered in the bed of a strange aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Desirable describes something widely wanted, which is what sought-after means.

clue.text: Confronts aristocrat hiding enemy of the revolution

indicators.note: the words hiding something conceal it within their letters

blocks.note: concealed across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone confronts a nobleman who is sheltering a counter-revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist supported the Russian monarchy and so opposed the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Find camper here with no-one about? That's the plan

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word faces the other way

blocks.note: a camper would be found in a tent
no plus one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Looking for an empty campsite: that is the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-one' is split into NO and I (one), then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or purpose, what one plans to do.

clue.text: Agents protecting City group

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one part wraps around another

blocks.note: spies are secret agents
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Secret agents guard a financial district group.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, whose postal district is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a group of related organisms, a classification category.

clue.text: Escape from court with errand boy

blocks.note: to see someone is to court or date them
a page is a boy who runs errands

explanation.surface: A messenger boy flees the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape' is a noun here, as in a leak of fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow leakage of liquid or gas, an escape of it.

clue.text: Must art lectures partly shock?

indicators.note: partly means only a portion, so the word is a stretch inside the phrase

blocks.note: concealed across the three words

explanation.surface: Do art lectures have to be so shocking?
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: Decided to pay off Democrat

blocks.note: to settle a bill is to pay it off
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A decision was made to bribe a Democrat politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay off' reads as bribe, but means settle a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled question is one that has been decided or resolved.

clue.text: US novelist articulating anger

indicators.note: articulating means pronouncing, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: wrath is fierce anger; in a British accent it rhymes with moth

explanation.surface: An American author voicing fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match works in British pronunciation, where wrath is said with a short o.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Roth was an American novelist, author of Portnoy's Complaint and American Pastoral.

clue.text: Follow suggestion

blocks.note: first meaning: to track or trail
second meaning: a faint hint or tiny amount

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice to take a hint; the words are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to track something down, and a trace is a very slight indication, like a suggestion of flavour.

clue.text: Others came down quite subdued

blocks.note: the rest are the others
rain comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: Other people arrived and were rather quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means held back and low-key, a close synonym of subdued.

clue.text: Stupid partners caught in the act? Not quite

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it
not quite complete means the last letter is missing

blocks.note: North and South are partners at bridge
a deed is an act; trim its final letter

explanation.surface: A dim couple were caught red-handed, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, North and South play as partners against East and West. 'Caught in the act' suggests red-handed; 'the act' alone is the source word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense, informally, means slow-witted or stupid.

clue.text: Model receiving £1,000 for spoof

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to model
K means a thousand, as in a 20K salary

explanation.surface: A model is paid a thousand pounds to take part in a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that parodies something, a spoof.

clue.text: Need protection after bruiser's first demand for money?

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: opening letter of bruiser
to lack is to need
chain mail is protective armour

explanation.surface: A thug demands payment for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the need and protection after the bruiser's first letter; the surface evokes a protection racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is a demand for payment in exchange for not revealing secrets.

clue.text: See fit to exclude head of state from plan

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
excluding something leaves it out

blocks.note: a design is a plan
first letter of state

explanation.surface: A leader decides to drop the head of state from the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend to do something, to consider it fitting to one's dignity.

clue.text: Employ specialist to dispose of piano

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: an expert is a specialist
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Hire a specialist to remove an old piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employ' looks like hire, but here means use, as in exert force.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert pressure or influence is to apply or employ it.

clue.text: Ran nude around church, showing guts

indicators.note: around suggests turning things about, so the letters are moved into new places

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A streaker ran naked around a church, a display of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts here means courage and staying power, close to endurance, the ability to keep going.
